info.description: # Azure Functions Python Library | Branch | CodeCov | |--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | master | [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/Azure/azure-functions-python-library/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/Azure/azure-functions-python-library) | | dev | [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/Azure/azure-functions-python-library/branch/dev/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/Azure/azure-functions-python-library) | ## Overview Python support for Azure Functions is based on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, and 3.15 serverless hosting on Linux, and the Functions 2.x ([EOL](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-versions?#retired-versions)), 3.x ([EOL](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-versions?#retired-versions)) and 4.0 runtime. Here is the current status of Python in Azure Functions: _What are the supported Python versions?_ | Azure Functions Runtime | Python 3.11 | Python 3.12 | Python 3.13 | Python 3.14 | Python 3.15 | |-------------------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------| | Azure Functions 4.0 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | _What's available?_ - Build, test, debug and publish using Azure Functions Core Tools (CLI) or Visual Studio Code - Triggers / Bindings : Blob, Cosmos DB, Event Grid, Event Hub, HTTP, Kafka, MySQL, Queue, ServiceBus, SQL, Timer, and Warmup - Create a Python Function on Linux using a custom docker image - Triggers / Bindings : Custom binding support #### Get Started - [Create your first Python function](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-create-first-function-python) - [Developer guide](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-reference-python) - [Binding API reference](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/python/api/azure-functions/azure.functions?view=azure-python) - [Develop using VS Code](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-create-first-function-vs-code) - [Create a Python Function on Linux using a custom docker image](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-create-function-linux-custom-image) #### Give Feedback Issues and feature requests are tracked in a variety of places. To report this feedback, please file an issue to the relevant repository below: | Item | Description | Link | |---------------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Python Worker | Programming Model, Triggers & Bindings | [File an Issue](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-python-worker/issues) | | Linux | Base Docker Images | [File an Issue](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-docker/issues) | | Runtime | Script Host & Language Extensibility | [File an Issue](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-host/issues) | | VSCode | VSCode Extension for Azure Functions | [File an Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-azurefunctions/issues) | | Core Tools | Command Line Interface for Local Development | [File an Issue](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-core-tools/issues) | | Portal | User Interface or Experience Issue | [File an Issue](https://github.com/azure/azure-functions-ux/issues) | | Templates | Code Issues with Creation Template | [File an Issue](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-templates/issues) | ## Durable Functions JSON serialization `azure.functions._durable_functions.df_dumps(value, *, ensure_ascii=True)` preserves legacy ASCII-escaped JSON by default. Pass `ensure_ascii=False` to opt in to emitting ordinary Unicode literally in either loose or strict typing mode. Surrogate code units, including lone surrogates and explicit surrogate-pair strings, remain JSON-escaped so the output is safe to encode as UTF-8 and pass through protobuf string fields. ASCII DEL also retains its legacy `\u007f` escape. Unicode is not normalized. ASCII output, whitespace, custom-object envelopes, and strict/loose type rules are unchanged; `df_loads` reads both escaped and literal-Unicode payloads. For the synthetic Python value `{"text": "\u0416" * 100000}` (100,000 Cyrillic characters), `df_dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)` produces **200,012 UTF-8 bytes**, compared with **600,012 bytes** using the default or explicit `ensure_ascii=True`. This isolates escaping overhead; it does not measure a complete production request or remove aggregate transport limits. **Opt-in compatibility:** Serialized bytes change for ordinary non-ASCII text only when selecting `ensure_ascii=False`, even though escaped and literal JSON decode to the same values. Applications deriving hashes, signatures, IDs, or replay decisions from serialized JSON must review their byte-dependent logic before opting in or switching back. Existing callers, including the activity trigger converter, continue to use ASCII-escaped output. Literal-Unicode output has not been validated against live hosted backends; provider integration/replay coverage and real-host staging validation are tracked in [microsoft/durabletask-python#291](https://github.com/microsoft/durabletask-python/issues/291), linked from [#371](https://github.com/Azure/azure-functions-python-library/issues/371). ## Contributing This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use your contribution.
